functionsUsed: WASM-SAFE subset: boost::format (->Rust format!/std::fmt), BOOST_LOG_TRIVIAL (->log crate), boost::property_tree ini/json (->serde_json + custom ini), boost::nowide (->std on wasm, UTF-8 native), boost::algorithm string split/trim/starts_with (->str methods/split), boost::multiprecision int128_t/int256_t/cpp_int (->i128/i256 via a tiny bigint), boost::variant (->Rust enum), boost::spirit grammar (->custom recursive-descent / nom), boost::container::small_vector (->smallvec), boost::object_pool (->typed-arena/Vec)

NOT-WASM-SAFE subset (must be feature-gated OUT of the wasm lib): boost::asio serial_port + boost::thread (GCodeSender), boost::process::child/system (PostProcessor), boost::dll::runtime_symbol_info (ToolOrdering), boost::filesystem real-FS + boost::log sinks::text_file_backend + boost::uuids::random_generator (LogSink/AppConfig)
libraries.proposedCrateName: bigint-i256 (only piece needing a vendored micro-crate)
libraries.recommendation: Boost splits cleanly. The header/algorithmic parts (format, log, string algos, variant, spirit grammar, containers, property_tree) are wasm-safe and already replaceable by std + log + serde_json + smallvec + a hand-written parser. The ONLY genuinely missing pure-Rust piece is boost::multiprecision int128_t/int256_t exact integer arithmetic used in Geometry/ConvexHull.cpp orientation predicates and GCode/ToolOrderUtils.cpp exact flow costs and MinAreaBoundingBox — i128 is native in Rust; for int256 vendor a tiny fixed-width signed 256-bit integer (add/sub/mul/compare/abs only). The OS/IO parts (asio serial port, process spawn, dll introspection, real filesystem, file-backed log, uuid RNG) are inherently non-wasm and must be feature-gated out of the browser build (the slicing core does not need them; they live in GCodeSender/PostProcessor/LogSink/AppConfig which are host-side concerns).

libraries.name: tbb
libraries.recommendation: Map parallel_for/blocked_range/parallel_reduce/parallel_for_each to rayon, spin_mutex to parking_lot::Mutex, concurrent_vector/map to Mutex<Vec>/Mutex<HashMap> or a sharded structure, max_concurrency to a constant. rayon compiles to wasm32 but does NOT actually parallelize without wasm threads, so provide a single-thread fallback (cfg(target_arch="wasm32") => sequential iter). The parallel_pipeline in the GCode exporter has no rayon primitive — implement as a sequential producer->consumer loop on wasm. Recommend a thin internal 'exec-shim' module (not a published crate) presenting parallel_for/reduce/pipeline that is rayon on native and sequential on wasm. No native linkage either way.

libraries.name: admesh
functionsUsed: indexed_triangle_set (vertices: Vec<Vec3f>, indices: Vec<Vec3i>) — used purely as a data type in most files
stl_fix_normal_directions / stl_validate (repair — NOT ported per STL.rs note)
libraries.recommendation: indexed_triangle_set is just a struct; define it natively. stl_io (pure Rust) covers stl_read/stl_write binary+ASCII (wasm-safe). The mesh-repair functions (stl_check_facets_exact/nearby vertex welding, fix_normal_directions) are small algorithms to port into a vendored 'its-mesh' helper (build edge map, weld coincident vertices, orient normals consistently). admesh's stl_repair is explicitly not ported. No native linkage.

libraries.name: miniz
functionsUsed: raw deflate/inflate for PNG zlib stream (RasterBase)
libraries.recommendation: zip 0.6 with features=["deflate"] uses flate2's pure-Rust rust_backend (miniz_oxide) — wasm-safe — and covers all mz_zip_* read/write needs incl. in-memory archives (init_mem/heap) for 3mf/AMF/SL1. For the raw zlib PNG stream in RasterBase use miniz_oxide directly. Do NOT enable zip's deflate-zlib/deflate-miniz features. No vendored crate required; just ensure the C++ staged-write API is mapped onto zip's writer.

libraries.name: expat
libraries.recommendation: expat is a SAX/streaming parser; quick-xml (pure Rust, wasm-safe) provides equivalent event-based reading (Reader::read_event => Start/End/Text) which maps 1:1 onto the start/end-element + character-data handler model used by 3mf/AMF parsing. Track line numbers via quick-xml's buffer position. No native linkage. Already a dependency.

libraries.name: nanosvg
functionsUsed: NSVGimage->shapes->paths traversal (NSVGshape, NSVGpath: pts cubic-bezier point list, fillRule, strokeWidth)
libraries.recommendation: Only the parse-and-walk surface is used (no rasterization except one nsvgRasterize site). Two routes: (a) adopt the pure-Rust 'usvg' crate (resvg project) which parses SVG into a shape/path tree — heavier but wasm-safe and well-maintained; or (b) vendor a minimal 'nanosvg-paths' crate that parses the SVG path 'd' attribute + basic shapes into cubic-bezier polylines with fillRule/lineJoin/lineCap, matching NSVGimage/NSVGshape/NSVGpath exactly (this mirrors what the C++ NSVGUtils consumes). Recommend (b) for a tight, dependency-light, byte-compatible result. Pure Rust, no linkage.

libraries.name: libpng
functionsUsed: read greyscale/RGB image from memory (png_file_in_memory_ex via custom read callback)
png write (PNGWriteRGB/Grey) for SLA raster + debug images
libraries.recommendation: Adopt the pure-Rust 'png' crate (uses miniz_oxide for the zlib stream, wasm-safe). It covers decode of grey/RGB and encode for SLA rasters and debug PNGs. The C++ only does simple 8-bit grey/RGB read+write, well within the png crate. No vendored crate needed; no native linkage.

libraries.name: libnest2d
functionsUsed: nest() with NfpPlacer + DJDHeuristic selection (2D bin packing / arrangement)
libraries.recommendation: libnest2d is header-only C++ template geometry (no system linkage) so it is wasm-portable but there is no Rust equivalent. Split usage: (1) minAreaBoundingBox/removeCollinearPoints/convexHull are small standalone algorithms — port into the geometry module (rotating calipers + Andrew monotone-chain hull; these are also already needed by Geometry/ConvexHull.cpp). (2) The full nest()/NfpPlacer/DJDHeuristic NoFitPolygon arrangement is the substantial piece — vendor a focused 'nest2d-rs' crate implementing only NFP placement + the DJD selection heuristic over Polygon inputs. Note libnest2d's optimizer backend historically used nlopt for rotation search; replicate that with the same derivative-free optimizer shim (see nlopt entry) so no native dep is pulled. Pure Rust, wasm-safe.

libraries.name: nlopt
functionsUsed: nlopt_create/destroy, set_lower_bounds/upper_bounds, set_min_objective/max_objective, set_ftol_abs/ftol_rel/stopval/maxeval, optimize, set_local_optimizer, force_stop, srand
algorithms actually used: NLOPT_LN_NELDERMEAD, NLOPT_LN_SBPLX (Subplex), NLOPT_GN_DIRECT, NLOPT_GN_ESCH (evolutionary), NLOPT_GN_MLSL (multi-level single-linkage, wraps a local optimizer)
libraries.currentRustCrate: none (the 'nlopt' crate on crates.io is a -sys binding to C nlopt, NOT wasm-safe)
libraries.recommendation: Only derivative-free optimizers are used (no gradient methods), all bound-constrained with simple stop criteria. Vendor a small pure-Rust 'derivfree-opt' crate implementing exactly: Nelder-Mead (LN_NELDERMEAD), Subplex (LN_SBPLX), DIRECT (GN_DIRECT), a simple evolutionary strategy (GN_ESCH), and MLSL as a multistart wrapper around the local optimizer (GN_MLSL + set_local_optimizer). Support set_lower/upper_bounds, min/max objective, ftol/stopval/maxeval, force_stop. These are textbook algorithms (~few hundred LOC each), no_std-friendly, no linkage. This unblocks arrange rotation search and SLA rotfinder/support widening for wasm.

libraries.name: glu-libtess
libraries.recommendation: Used in exactly one file to triangulate ExPolygons (polygons with holes) into a triangle list with the nonzero winding rule. Options: adopt the existing pure-Rust 'tess2'/'libtess2'-port crate if available, otherwise vendor a minimal 'libtess-rs' implementing the SGI tessellation (or simpler: since inputs are already simple polygons-with-holes from Clipper, a constrained ear-clipping / monotone-polygon triangulation with hole-bridging is sufficient and far smaller). Pure Rust, wasm-safe. Overlaps with the CGAL CDT need (Triangulation.cpp) — a single robust 2D triangulator could serve both.

libraries.name: CGAL
functionsUsed: Exact_predicates_exact_constructions_kernel + segment intersection/orientation predicates (VoronoiUtilsCgal.cpp — exact Voronoi validation)
libraries.recommendation: Split by dimension. (1) The 2D Constrained Delaunay Triangulation (Triangulation.cpp) is wasm-safe and replaceable: adopt the pure-Rust 'spade' crate (CDT with vertex info) or vendor 'cdt2d'; spatial_sort is just a Hilbert/Morton presort. (2) VoronoiUtilsCgal exact predicates: replace with exact orientation/segment-intersection predicates using i128/i256 (Shewchuk-style or exact integer) — small, wasm-safe, no CGAL. (3) The hard part is 3D mesh boolean via PMP::corefine (CutSurface/MeshBoolean). There is no mature pure-Rust corefinement boolean. Recommend vendoring a 'mesh-corefine' crate implementing triangle-triangle intersection + corefinement + inside/outside classification for union/diff/intersect — significant effort; share this single implementation across CGAL, libigl mesh_boolean, AND mcut needs (they are three interchangeable backends for the same operation). Feature-gate CSG/cut behind it so the rest of the slicer ships to wasm even before this lands.

libraries.name: libigl
functionsUsed: igl::Hit — POD struct {int id; int gid; float t; float u; float v;} used 30x as a ray-hit record ONLY (no libigl code)
igl::copyleft::cgal::mesh_boolean (MeshBoolean.cpp — wraps CGAL, same as CGAL entry)
libraries.recommendation: Most 'libigl' usage is NOT libigl: igl::Hit is a trivial 5-field struct — define it locally, no crate. igl::copyleft::cgal::mesh_boolean is just the CGAL boolean backend (covered by the 'mesh-corefine' crate above). The only genuine libigl algorithms are the subdivision functions in TriangleMeshDeal.cpp (igl::loop = Loop subdivision, igl::upsample = midpoint upsample, false_barycentric_subdivision) — vendor a tiny pure-Rust 'mesh-subdiv' crate replicating exactly those three on an indexed_triangle_set. All wasm-safe, no linkage. Note TriangleMeshDeal.rust is currently null (not yet ported).

libraries.name: mcut
libraries.recommendation: mcut is an ALTERNATIVE mesh-boolean backend to CGAL/libigl (PerformCSGMeshBooleans picks one). It is pure C++ (no system deps) so theoretically wasm-portable, but maintaining a C++ kernel under wasm defeats the no-cc goal. Do NOT vendor mcut separately — collapse all three boolean backends (CGAL corefine, libigl mesh_boolean, mcut dispatch) into the single pure-Rust 'mesh-corefine' crate. Only one robust corefinement implementation is needed. Feature-gate until ready.

libraries.name: qhull
functionsUsed: QhullFacetList / QhullVertexSet iteration — used ONLY in its_convex_hull (3D convex hull of Vec3f points -> indexed_triangle_set)
libraries.recommendation: qhull is used for exactly one thing: 3D convex hull (its_convex_hull / TriangleMesh::convex_hull_3d). 2D convex hull already goes through Slic3r::Geometry::convex_hull (no qhull). Vendor a minimal pure-Rust 'convexhull3d' implementing the QuickHull 3D algorithm returning an indexed_triangle_set, or adopt an existing pure-Rust quickhull crate (e.g. 'chull'). Small, wasm-safe, no linkage. qhull's general d-dimensional/Delaunay/Voronoi features are unused.

libraries.name: openvdb
libraries.recommendation: openvdb is huge but only a narrow level-set subset is used: voxelize a mesh into a narrow-band signed-distance FloatGrid, do CSG by min/max combination of level sets, rebuild/redistance, and mesh back via marching cubes; plus closest-surface-point for hollowing. There is no Rust port of OpenVDB. Vendor a focused 'levelset-vdb' crate: a sparse (hash-grid/tile) narrow-band SDF, meshToVolume via scan-conversion of triangles, csgUnion/Difference/Intersection as voxelwise min/-/max, levelSetRebuild via fast-sweeping redistance, and volumeToMesh via marching cubes. Note TreeSupport3D.rust already replaced the organic-branch meshing with a tube mesher (branch_mesh.rs), reducing openvdb need there. This is wasm-safe pure Rust but a meaningful build; feature-gate Hollowing/voxel-CSG until ready.

libraries.name: opencv
functionsUsed: cv::kmeans (KMEANS_PP_CENTERS init, TermCriteria, theRNG) — color quantization clustering
cv::Mat / cv::Vec3b — used only as pixel/data containers
cv::cvtColor with COLOR_RGB2Lab / RGB2HSV (color-space conversion before clustering)
libraries.recommendation: opencv is used in ONE header for OBJ vertex-color quantization only. Nothing imaging/CV-heavy. Vendor a tiny pure-Rust 'kmeans-color' crate: k-means++ initialization + Lloyd iterations over RGB/Lab/HSV vectors with a max-iter/epsilon TermCriteria, plus the 3 color-space conversions (RGB<->Lab, RGB<->HSV). cv::Mat/Vec are replaced by Vec<[f32;3]>. ~150 LOC, wasm-safe, no linkage. This removes the entire opencv dependency.

libraries.name: agg (Anti-Grain Geometry)
libraries.recommendation: Used only to rasterize SLA layer ExPolygons into an 8-bit greyscale mask with anti-aliasing + gamma. Vendor a small pure-Rust 'agg-gray-raster' crate: a scanline AA polygon rasterizer (nonzero/even-odd) writing to a Vec<u8> gray8 buffer with a gamma function — this is the classic AGG scanline algorithm in a few hundred LOC. Alternatively adopt an existing pure-Rust AA rasterizer (e.g. the rasterizer in 'raqote'/'tiny-skia' style), but a dedicated micro-crate keeps output byte-identical to the SLA pipeline. wasm-safe, no linkage.

libraries.name: openssl
libraries.currentRustCrate: none (openssl crate is a -sys binding, NOT wasm-safe)
libraries.recommendation: openssl is used ONLY to AES-256-CBC encrypt Bambu cloud log payloads in LogSink — a host/telemetry concern, not slicing. Preferred: feature-gate this out of the wasm library entirely (the browser slicer does not produce encrypted cloud logs). If the function must exist, replace with the pure-Rust RustCrypto stack: 'aes' + 'cbc' crates (block cipher + CBC mode), which are pure Rust and wasm-safe. Do not use the openssl/-sys crate.

libraries.name: OpenCASCADE (OCCT)
functionsUsed: BRepMesh_IncrementalMesh + BRep_Tool::Triangulation + Poly_Triangulation (tessellate B-rep to triangles)
libraries.recommendation: This is the hardest dependency: a full B-rep/NURBS CAD kernel with a font engine. There is NO pure-Rust equivalent and porting OCCT is infeasible. Scope decision: STEP import, SVG-to-solid extrusion, and OCCT text-shape are NOT core FDM slicing. Recommendation: feature-gate STEP.rs / format/svg.rs OCCT path / shape/text_shape.rs OUT of the wasm build so the slicer ships without them; STEP/text remain native-only (host pre-converts STEP->STL/3MF before handing to wasm). If STEP import is truly required in-browser long-term, vendor a narrow 'step-brep-reader' that parses STEP AP203/214, evaluates only the surface types actually present, and tessellates — a large, separate effort. Mark non-wasm for now.

libraries.name: Apple ModelIO (Objective-C .mm)
functionsUsed: exportToURL (export mesh to STL via Apple frameworks)
libraries.recommendation: Apple-platform-only Objective-C bridge for mesh import/export via the ModelIO framework. Inherently non-wasm and non-portable (links Apple system frameworks). Feature-gate to cfg(target_os="macos") and exclude from the wasm/library surface. STL/OBJ/3MF readers already cover the formats needed; ModelIO is redundant for the cross-platform/wasm build. No replacement crate — drop for wasm.

libraries.name: cereal
libraries.recommendation: cereal is C++ (de)serialization used for in-app undo/redo snapshots and ObjectID. Pure logic, wasm-safe. Replace with serde derive (already a dependency) + a binary format such as 'bincode' for the snapshot use cases (or serde_json where human-readable is fine). No vendored crate; no linkage.

libraries.name: fast_float
libraries.recommendation: fast_float is just a fast locale-independent float parser. Rust's std f64::from_str is already locale-independent and wasm-safe; use it directly (or the pure-Rust 'lexical-core' if matching fast_float's exact perf/rounding is needed). No vendored crate, no linkage.

libraries.name: nlohmann_json
libraries.recommendation: Direct map to serde_json (already a dependency, pure Rust, wasm-safe). No vendored crate, no linkage.

A map record keyed on the C++ filename cannot point at both; whichever it points at, the other is unexplained, and if it points at the stub the record is false-done.

gcode/generator.rs (1455L, the module most plausibly mapped to GCode.cpp) is NOT referenced anywhere outside itself - the live emitter is gcode::exporter (orphan). So a record 'GCode.cpp -> gcode/generator.rs status=done' would describe dead code, not the executing path.
Stub modules are still pub-exported from lib.rs (rust!=null) yet are functionally missing - a record showing rust=<path>, status=done would contradict the in-file STATUS=Stub banner.
critic.verdict: The biggest risk to EXACT gcode parity is that the map almost certainly overstates completeness because the crate ships two parallel module trees and ~70 modules (including core slicing/path files PrintObjectSlice, ShortestPath, FlushVolCalc/FlushVolPredictor, OverhangDetector, the entire SLA subtree, and the flat Point/Polygon/ExPolygon/ExtrusionEntityCollection set) are explicit auto-generated 'Stub placeholder - implementation needed' files still pub-exported from lib.rs. The reported 'orphans' list is unreliable: most entries are not orphans but the redundant/competing half of a flat-vs-hierarchical duplicate pair, masking which implementation is authoritative. Most dangerously, the executing gcode emitter is gcode::exporter (a 3085-line orphan with no C++ source mapping) invoked by Print::export_gcode, while gcode/generator.rs (the file that would be mapped to GCode.cpp) is dead/unreferenced and gcode/reader.rs is a 19-line stub shadowing the real 1081-line gcode_reader.rs. Because exact byte-for-byte gcode depends on toolpath ordering (ShortestPath - stubbed), seam placement, flush/purge volumes (FlushVolCalc - stubbed), cooling/pressure-equalizer, arc-fitting and placeholder-parser interactions, and the live emitter is an unmapped reimplementation rather than a verified port of GCode.cpp/GCodeWriter.cpp, parity cannot be assured from the current map. Priority-weighted real completeness is ~45 percent: geometry/perimeter/surface/fill/arachne/support hierarchical trees are substantively implemented (1000-3000 line files), but the gcode-determining tail and many 1:1 'done' records resolve to stubs or to a parallel emitter the map does not track. Recommended next steps: (1) collapse the duplicate trees and mark which module is authoritative per C++ file; (2) re-classify every file whose Rust target contains the stub banner as missing/partial; (3) re-key the GCode.cpp/GCodeWriter.cpp records onto gcode::exporter and audit it line-by-line, since it is the only path that actually produces output.
